transcript:
MEETING HEADER
Date: 2027-01-29
Start: 16:00 UTC | Duration: ~62 minutes
Attendees: Sofia Patel (Redwood AE), Marcus Lee (Redwood SE), Aisha Khan (Redwood CSM); Daniel Park (HelioMetrics), Ruth Gomez (HelioMetrics), Liam O'Connor (HelioMetrics)

SUMMARY:
Quick QBR-style health check to align on usage trends, cost hotspots during peak inference, readiness for the pilot, and security/compliance blocking items. Agreed to run a 24h perf/cost test and exchange updated SOW and security artifacts.

TOPICS:
- Current production usage and hour-by-hour latency spikes
- Dedicated vs hosted sizing for peak 95th percentile
- KMS/HSM and VPC access for pilot
- Rollout plan and SLA expectations
- Cost optimization levers (batching, quant, cache)

LINKS SHARED:
- Redwood pricing deck (redwood.com/pilot/pricing-deck) [note: placeholder link]
- Pilot SOW draft (will be shared after call)
- Security pack (SOC2 summary + PCI matrix) (to be shared)

TRANSCRIPT:
[00:00] Sofia Patel: hey everyone thanks for joining on a friday afternoon, we'll kick off — i'm sofia from redwood, and with me is marcus and aisha. how's everyone's morning/afternoon?
[00:12] Daniel Park: good thanks sofia, busy week but glad to sync. we wanted this to be a compact QBR + operational handoff before we kick off the pilot.
[00:20] Marcus Lee: yeah i'll try to keep the deep perf bits organized. quick agenda: usage, pain points, pilot sizing, security, then action items. sound good?
[00:30] Liam O'Connor: yeah perfect.

[01:05] Ruth Gomez: i pulled some hour-by-hour metrics, we're seeing big spikes around 11am and 7pm local; tail latency goes up and token cost jumps, so want to understand if that's our wrong config or something on your side
[01:25] Marcus Lee: ok quick q — are those bursts mostly short-lived fan-outs (like 30s) or multi-minute sustained traffic?
[01:36] Ruth Gomez: it's usually 3–8 minutes, last week one was 22 minutes. it's correlated with our batch job that ships notifications.
[02:05] Marcus Lee: that explains a lot — continuous batching is better for throughput but for short bursts you want smaller max-batch windows and prefix caching. we can show a config that keeps 95th p90 under x ms while reducing per-token cost.

[03:00] Daniel Park: on cost, our finance team flagged Feb budget if we don't show savings. is dedicated reserved capacity the only way to get predictable unit cost?
[03:18] Sofia Patel: not the only way — dedicated gives predictability for sustained throughput. for variable workloads we often recommend a hybrid: reserved baseline + burst shared hosted. That gives a lower committed unit plus overflow.
[03:40] Liam O'Connor: any numbers you can ballpark for our 500 reqs/min peak? rough tflop or GPU counts?
[03:50] Marcus Lee: rough estimate: for a 7b-like open model, sustained 500 rpm with avg seq of 256 is in the 8–12 RTX class depending on quantization. we'll dimension precisely during the perf run.

[05:10] Aisha Khan: quick note on governance — you'll want SSO, RBAC, and audit logs; we can enable per-route tokens and long term retention in enterprise tier.
[05:30] Ruth Gomez: yes SOC2 and KMS integration are blockers for our security team, they asked for HSM options too.
[05:45] Sofia Patel: we support customer-managed KMS and HSM integrations for private; for hosted we offer envelope encryption and bring-your-own-key for dedicated/private offers. we'll include the exact KMS flow in the security pack.

[07:20] Daniel Park: regarding on-prem vs vpc — we prefer VPC peering to start, on-prem only if needed later. what's the network setup required?
[07:35] Marcus Lee: for VPC we need a transit gateway + peering config; we can provide a terraform snippet. If you want private control plane, that moves to the private deployment option with extra checklist (firewalls, NATs, certs).

[09:00] Liam O'Connor: about rollout — can we do canary for a subset of users? we can't afford full production cutover.
[09:15] Sofia Patel: absolutely. standard pattern: 1% canary -> 10% -> 50% with automatic rollback on latency or error regression. Redwood console has built-in canary policies and auto-fallback to previous model.

[11:50] Ruth Gomez: one more on observability: token-level cost mapping is critical. current logs from our app don't include full prompt size, we may need to augment.
[12:05] Marcus Lee: we can instrument SDK to emit prompt token counts, and there's a tokenization helper in the SDK. also we can push trace hooks so you can map tokens -> cost per route.

[14:00] Daniel Park: ok, what about caching — you mentioned prefix and KV cache earlier — is KV cache safe for PII?
[14:19] Marcus Lee: kv cache is for non-sensitive tokens usually, if you have PII we treat cached elements as sensitive; the platform can encrypt cache with customer KMS keys, or disable KV caching for routes that might contain PII.
[14:45] Ruth Gomez: ah ok good to know. security team will want that documented.

[17:30] Liam O'Connor: competitor question — our infra team asks why not use our internal self-hosted stack vs using redwood dedicated endpoints.
[17:45] Sofia Patel: common question — biggest tradeoff is ops overhead vs performance/cost. internal self-hosting can be cheaper if you 100% utilize capacity and manage kernel perf; Redwood reduces time-to-market, provides pre-optimized kernels and autoscaling, and handles rollouts and observability.
[18:15] Daniel Park: and latency? we've had issues hitting tails under 300ms.
[18:28] Marcus Lee: with the right model shard and batching, we hit sub-200ms for a lot of workloads. we'll validate on your sample and share p95/p99 numbers.

[22:00] (discussion moves into pilot scope details)
[22:12] Sofia Patel: proposed pilot: 3 months, reserved baseline for business hours, burst to hosted, evaluation criteria: p95 latency under X, cost per 1M tokens under $Y, no security exceptions. will share SOW.
[22:40] Ruth Gomez: timeline constraint — finance needs a signed commitment by 02/15 to include in monthly forecast.
[23:00] Sofia Patel: ok we'll aim to get pricing and SOW by 02/02 to give your procurement time.

[26:10] Marcus Lee: technical checklist for pilot: sample traffic profile, anonymized dataset, network egress rules, service account/iam for KMS. Ruth, can you provide the traffic profile CSV?
[26:25] Ruth Gomez: yes i can pull that and send by friday — will redact PII.
[26:40] Marcus Lee: perfect. i'll plan a 24h perf run with that profile and push results and cost modeling.

[29:50] (brief silence, then crosstalk)
[30:15] Daniel Park: on the SLA — for dedicated do you have uptime and latency targets? our legal team wants specifics.
[30:28] Aisha Khan: dedicated has a 99.95% uptime SLA on the infra and SLO targets we can include; for latency we provide per-route SLOs and can add a financial credit table for enterprise contracts.

[33:40] Liam O'Connor: for pilot acceptance, is there an objective quality gate? like automated evals?
[33:55] Marcus Lee: yes we can wire in evaluations — take a holdout prompt set and compare output quality across model variants and quant settings. we'll report fuzziness/regression besides the latency/cost metrics.

[36:10] Ruth Gomez: curious about quantization — do you recommend int8 for our use case? we rely on some compositional reasoning.
[36:25] Marcus Lee: quantization can reduce cost ~2–3x but some higher-order reasoning can degrade. we'll test both 8-bit and 4-bit quant profiles and surface differences in the evals. often a mixed approach works — use higher precision for critical routes, quantize others.

[40:00] Sofia Patel: quick check — procurement and legal asks: standard indemnity and data residency clauses; do you need a POPA? (point of protection?)
[40:12] Liam O'Connor: they asked for data residency controls, yes.
[40:20] Sofia Patel: we can include data residency options in dedicated/private offers and the security pack will show certs and region controls.

[43:30] Daniel Park: any blockers you see from redwood side to start pilot mid feb?
[43:40] Marcus Lee: only blocker is the traffic/profile + KMS access notionally — otherwise we can schedule perf run and kick the canary plan. security docs we'll send this week.

[46:50] Ruth Gomez: one more technical — how do rollbacks behave if we exceed tail latency? automatic rollback or circuit-break?
[47:05] Marcus Lee: automatic rollback is supported; we also have per-route circuit break thresholds and can configure graceful degradation to smaller model variants when saturated.

[50:10] (wrap-up)
[50:30] Sofia Patel: recap — action items: we'll send pricing + SOW by 02/02, security pack by 02/01, marcus will run perf test and share spreadsheet by 02/08, ruth will provide traffic and sample data by 02/03. schedule follow-up on 02/11 to review perf.
[50:58] Liam O'Connor: that works, appreciate the clear dates.

[51:30] Daniel Park: any immediate risks from our side? i'd say procurement timeline, but we have a green path if finance signs.
[51:45] Aisha Khan: we'll hand off to CSM once pilot sign is in place; aisha will run onboarding and ensure the runbooks are in place.
[52:05] Aisha Khan: yes i'll coordinate runbooks and onboarding docs.

[55:00] (small talk)
[55:30] Marcus Lee: quick note — i'll include a sample terraform snippet for VPC peering and a minimal egress rule set.
[55:45] Ruth Gomez: great, that's helpful.

[58:10] Sofia Patel: thanks everyone, we'll follow up in email with the deck and SOW. any last questions?
[58:22] Daniel Park: none from me, thanks.
[58:35] Liam O'Connor: thanks.
[58:45] Ruth Gomez: thanks all.

[61:00] Sofia Patel: thanks, end.

MEETING RECAP (auto):
- Pilot agreed: 3 months with baseline reserved + burst. Acceptance criteria: p95 latency + cost target + no security exceptions.
- Next steps and owners listed in action items.

NOTES ON TRANSCRIPTION QUALITY:
- Some product names (KMS/HSM, KV cache) may be mis-capitalized or split ("K M S" vs KMS). Proper nouns occasionally wrong.

END OF TRANSCRIPT
